# ARCH-17: Libraries carry no vehicle-specific code; the vehicle moderates them

- A library serves every vehicle, including ones that do not use a feature today but may tomorrow, and a library with vehicle-specific code has to be built once per vehicle, which slows every multi-vehicle build. So a library never tests at run time which vehicle it is in: behaviour that differs by vehicle lives in the vehicle's code, which moderates the library through a mechanism the library offers - a setter, an option, or a generic signal the vehicle sets for itself (`get_fly_forward()`, `takeoff_expected()`).
- Compiling part of a library out of one vehicle's build (`APM_BUILD_TYPE`) is the exception: only for something that could never make sense on that vehicle, only where strictly necessary, and the PR says why and what Replay, built as its own vehicle type, then does with that vehicle's logs. [#34292](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/pull/34292) compiled a landing floor out of Rover, which never lands, rather than take a runtime vehicle-class test.

Confirmed 2026-10-16. Part of the root playbook, under [Architectural Principles](../claude/CLAUDE.md#architectural-principles). [All architectural rules](../README.md#architectural-rules)
